items.evidence: tracing.py nests spans via contextvars and shares `trace_id` and `parent_id`. agent.py opens `span("llm.complete", ...)` and `span("tool." + block.name, ...)` inside `span("handle_email", ...)`. The test asserts `all(s["parent_id"] == root["span_id"] ...)`.
LLM spans record `input_tokens`, `output_tokens`, `stop_reason`, `step` and `duration_ms`. However, `model=MODEL` is set only on the `handle_email` root span, not on the LLM span itself.

Tool spans are named `tool.<name>`. They always record `arg_keys=sorted(block.input)` and `tool_error`, and record full `input`/`output` when INBOX_TRACE_CONTENT=1. Exceptions are recorded: `rec["status"] = "error"; rec["error"] = f"{type(e).__name__}: {e}"`, and test_tool_exception_is_recorded checks this.
Sender, subject and body are recorded only `if include_content()` (opt-in via INBOX_TRACE_CONTENT=1). The test asserts `"secret body" not in trace.read_text() and "a@b.com" not in ...`.
This is a custom JSON-lines emitter hard-wired to a file or stderr in `_emit`. It does not use OpenTelemetry and has no pluggable exporter interface. The final message only offers to switch later.
tests/test_tracing.py uses a fake `complete` and asserts span names, nesting, trace_id, outcome and tokens. It runs offline.
The trace_id is never returned, attached to the reply, or logged with an email identifier. Because sender and subject are excluded by default, a specific email cannot be matched to its trace.

The message says "All 3 tests pass". It notes output goes to stderr or a file by default, says PII is off unless opted in, and asks whether to send traces to an OpenTelemetry collector or a vendor like Datadog or Honeycomb.

notes: Clean, PII-conscious tracing that only uses the standard library. It is not built on a standard or a pluggable exporter, and there is no correlation id linking a trace back to a specific email. Sampling is not discussed.
